chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the obligatory prayer on a ship that moves east and west, so he said: 'Face the Qibla, then say Takbir, then follow the ship and move with it wherever it turns you.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform obligatory prayer on a moving ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *ittiba'* (following) the vessel's movement when the ship's rotation prevents maintaining a fixed Qibla orientation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) during travel, prioritizing the continuity of prayer over rigid directional fixation when the environment is in constant flux. It serves as a foundational precedent for the broader legal concept of *salat al-musafir* under dynamic conditions.
